I reviewed the current code at **`2657601`**, the official hackathon requirements, and both platforms’ documentation.

**My recommendation: integrate Entire Graph into AgentForge’s coding tools, and connect CFO.ai through the existing MCP plugin system.** Use the resulting measurements to build AgentForge’s business plan in CFO.ai.

The hackathon requires Entire to help build or improve the agent and CFO.ai to model pricing, costs, revenue, and runway. It accepts Entire checkpoints **or graph output** as evidence; embedding every sponsor product into the runtime is unnecessary. [Official requirements](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)

| Tool | Best role in AgentForge | Concrete use case |
|---|---|---|
| **Entire Graph** | Help the coding agent locate code and understand dependencies | “Fix this issue, identify affected callers, and test the relevant behavior.” |
| **CFO.ai** | Build and compare financial models through chat | “Using our operating costs, compare pricing plans and show margins and runway.” |
| **Neatlogs** | Measure execution and prove improvements | Compare the same coding task before and after adding Entire. |

**Entire should improve how the agent understands repositories.**

AgentForge already loads a selected repository into a persistent E2B workspace and provides `grep`, file reads, edits, shell execution, and PR delivery. Entire can provide focused repository context before those operations. Its graph supports ranked search, definitions, callers, and change impact, with source locations; its built-in analysis runs locally without model calls. [Entire Graph](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph)

I recommend this implementation:

1. **Package a pinned Entire CLI and Graph version in the E2B template.** Avoid installing them during individual conversations.
2. **Expose three small, typed tools:** proposed names `search_code_context`, `inspect_code_symbol`, and `analyze_change_impact`. Execute the corresponding CLI operations inside the conversation’s existing sandbox.
3. **Register them through the existing tool catalog and telemetry wrappers.** The integration belongs beside [sandbox tools](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/tools/sandbox_shell.py:181), wired through [runtime composition](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/bootstrap.py:47).
4. **Update the existing coding skills** to query the graph, read the indicated source, make changes, and run tests. Continue using ordinary search when graph coverage is incomplete.
5. **Bound execution and output.** Return relevant symbols, snippets, file locations, and coverage warnings. Keep generated caches outside publishable source changes.

Queries must reflect the current workspace. Entire distinguishes working-tree queries from committed-tree queries; a committed index must not silently serve results for subsequent edits. Pin the version and verify its actual command interface—the current documentation and repository examples differ in some command names. [Graph command reference](https://docs.entire.io/cli-reference/graph)

There is one important constraint in our implementation: [repository loading](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/tools/sandbox_shell.py:129) uploads a snapshot and creates a new local Git repository with a synthetic base commit. **Entire can analyze that code, but it cannot recover the original repository’s commit history from this snapshot.** History-based explanations and historical co-change analysis would require a separate history integration.

I would defer automatic Entire checkpoint capture. AgentForge runs a custom Python agent loop, so native session capture needs a deliberate adapter through Entire’s Agent Integration Protocol. Graph integration provides immediate value without exporting conversation transcripts. [Custom-agent integration](https://docs.entire.io/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview)

**CFO.ai should use our existing plugin infrastructure.**

CFO.ai exposes an official remote MCP endpoint:

`https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`

It supports inspecting and modifying financial models, scenarios, tables, formulas, and pages. AgentForge already has remote MCP connections, OAuth, encrypted credentials, per-conversation plugin selection, and tool approvals. [CFO.ai MCP documentation](https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server)

I also tested **unauthenticated OAuth discovery through AgentForge’s own code**: it successfully recognized CFO.ai’s resource and authorization metadata. Authenticated tool calls remain unverified.

The implementation should be:

1. **Qualify it first as a custom plugin**, then add a CFO.ai entry to the [plugin catalog](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/plugins/catalog.py:43) after the complete OAuth flow passes.
2. **Select and retain the intended workspace.** Use `list_orgs`, then consistently supply the selected `org_id`. For a dedicated finance workflow, enforce that binding in code.
3. **Add a financial-planning skill** that inspects existing models, reads CFO.ai’s `build-model` instructions, creates an alternative scenario, updates assumptions, and reads calculated results back.
4. **Start with a focused tool selection:** workspace discovery, model inspection, scenarios, tables, and pages. Add integrations and automation only when needed.
5. **Reuse existing approval behavior** for writes, with a clear workspace/scenario preview. After an uncertain write timeout, inspect the saved model before retrying.

CFO.ai requires one action block per multi-action call and recommends inspecting existing content before editing it. Its scenario mechanism supports exploring an alternative without changing Main. [Agent instructions](https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions), [Scenario workflow](https://docs.cfo.ai/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios)

A specific compatibility gap needs attention: our [MCP initialization code](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/plugins/mcp.py:312) currently discards server-provided `instructions`. CFO.ai supplies modeling guidance during initialization. We should preserve bounded, clearly scoped guidance or encode the reviewed workflow in our own skill.

**Our cost export needs correction before it feeds the business plan.**

The existing [business metrics exporter](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/operations/business_metrics.py:13) is a useful starting point, but it is not complete unit economics:

- Sandbox and plugin adapters report zero tool cost, which does not establish that their external services are free.
- It omits hosting, payment fees, support, and revenue.
- It identifies unknown costs using `cost_usd IS NULL`, but [budget recording](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/budget.py:181) stores an authorized upper bound in that field when actual cost is unknown. Consequently, the exporter can label estimates as measured costs.

Fix the export to distinguish **measured usage, configured-rate estimates, conservative bounds, and untracked costs**. Add E2B lifecycle costs, task outcomes, retries, and cost distributions. Keep this cross-user aggregate operator-only.

Then use CFO.ai to compare subscription-plus-usage and usage-based pricing, with base and downside scenarios. Include failed attempts and heavy users when evaluating margins; leave unmeasured inputs explicitly labeled as assumptions.

**The strongest demo connects all three tools to one result.**

Run the same repository task with and without Entire, keeping the model, starting commit, and acceptance tests consistent. Use Neatlogs to compare correctness, context consumption, tool calls, latency, and cost—including graph startup overhead. Then put the measured difference into CFO.ai and show its effect on AgentForge’s pricing and margins.

That gives each integration a clear purpose: **Entire improves repository understanding; Neatlogs measures the improvement; CFO.ai shows whether the product can sustain its operating costs.**

Research only: no code changes, installations, account connections, or server/tunnel restarts were performed.

<proposed_plan>
# Production integration plan: Entire Graph and CFO.ai

## 1. Outcome, decisions, and implementation baseline

Extend AgentForge with two useful capabilities:

- **Repository understanding:** Entire Graph helps the coding agent find implementations, inspect symbols, and assess change impact before editing.
- **Financial planning:** Users connect their own CFO.ai account and create inspectable pricing, cost, revenue, margin, and runway models through AgentForge.

The hackathon demonstration will connect these capabilities: complete a coding task, measure the effect of Entire using Neatlogs, and use the measured operating costs in AgentForge’s CFO.ai business plan. This directly supports the sponsor requirements and improvement evidence requested by the [official hackathon rules](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon).

**Confirmed product decisions**

- CFO.ai is available to all users through their own accounts.
- The first release focuses on financial planning, not finance-system administration.
- Finance writes follow the current **Ask me / Approve for me** behavior.
- Changes default to a separate CFO.ai scenario. Main requires explicit user selection.
- Entire Graph is available automatically for selected repositories, but analysis runs only when needed.
- Entire transcript capture, checkpoints, repository hosting, and Brain are deferred.

**Verified baseline**

The reviewed checkout is based on `2657601` and includes existing uncommitted repository, sandbox, and activity changes. Preserve those changes. The focused baseline suite passed **234 tests** covering plugins, OAuth, sandbox tools, delivery workspace behavior, and skills.

The implementation must address these source-confirmed gaps:

| Existing behavior | Required addition |
|---|---|
| E2B contains a repository snapshot with a synthetic base commit | Graph analysis must distinguish current source from unavailable upstream history |
| MCP connections are already per-user, with OAuth and encrypted credentials | CFO.ai needs explicit workspace/scenario binding and provider-specific validation |
| MCP initialization discards server instructions | Preserve bounded guidance without granting it additional authority |
| Plugin results are shortened before durable storage | Preserve complete bounded results and financial receipts for later inspection |
| External write failures can return ordinary retryable-looking errors | CFO.ai needs durable operation tracking and uncertain-outcome handling |
| Business metrics treat some upper bounds as measured costs | Correct cost provenance and disclose missing infrastructure costs |

No local software installation, server restart, tunnel change, or account modification is part of planning. Future implementation uses the existing development environment and a separately built E2B template.

## 2. Entire Graph: sandbox integration

### Runtime and packaging

- Add a trusted Graph adapter beside the existing sandbox tools, using the same `ConversationSandbox` and task authorization.
- Package the Entire CLI and Graph binary into a new, versioned E2B template. Do not download or upgrade binaries during conversations.
- Use CLI `v0.11.4` and Graph commit `f22e6c952f3b375261942e6a17af67ca6b1d2e39` as the qualification candidates identified during research. Record release archive checksums, source revision, licenses, and the resulting template/build identifiers.
- Treat the Graph candidate as unqualified until its executable passes the compatibility and security tests below. Do not substitute a floating `latest` release.
- Retain the existing template for rollback. Existing sandboxes continue running unchanged; if they lack Graph, ordinary coding tools remain available.
- Probe Graph version and capabilities once per sandbox attachment. Construction of the agent runtime must remain free of remote provisioning.

The adapter will use only local analysis commands. It will not enable Entire hooks, modify repository instructions, capture transcripts, or mirror repositories. Entire documents these analysis and execution boundaries separately. [Entire security model](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/main/docs/trust-and-security.md)

### Agent-facing tools

Expose three typed tools:

| Tool | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `code_graph_search` | Task/query text, optional relative directory, result limit | Ranked source locations and bounded snippets |
| `code_graph_symbol` | Symbol name, optional relative file for disambiguation | Definition and supported direct relationships |
| `code_graph_impact` | Symbol reference, depth of 1–2 | Affected callers, callees, consumers, and coverage warnings |

Common result metadata includes repository identity, original source commit, working-tree view, Graph version, duration, truncation, exclusions, and partial-analysis warnings.

Implementation rules:

- Bind repository and workspace server-side; the model cannot supply arbitrary filesystem roots, executable paths, environment variables, or CLI flags.
- Use fixed command templates and correctly quoted arguments. Parse machine-readable output wherever supported; never parse source-containing text as executable instructions.
- Default to 10 search results, an approximately 8 KB model preview, and a 60-second analysis deadline. Store larger bounded results through existing context-resource retrieval.
- Reuse existing repository size limits and disclose exclusions rather than silently presenting partial analysis as complete.
- Classify these as controlled read tools requiring sandbox-read permission. They must not grant arbitrary shell execution to a research subagent.
- Add the names to contracts, capability checks, descriptions, custom-agent tool choices, and a new immutable built-in agent version. Preserve historical agent definitions and running task snapshots.

### Freshness and failure behavior

Analyze the **working tree**, including edits. Do not create synthetic commits simply to make caching possible.

Entire’s current working-tree analysis does not reuse its committed-tree search cache. Avoid introducing a second persistent cache in this release. Set its cache directory outside publishable source files. [Entire cache semantics](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/main/docs/operations.md)

- Attribute returned source evidence to content hashes and the time of analysis.
- Detect changes to cited files during analysis; retry once, then return a stale-result warning if concurrent edits continue.
- Require the agent to read current source before editing. Graph relationships remain supporting evidence, not proof of correctness.
- On unsupported languages, missing binaries, timeout, incomplete parsing, or provider failure, return a clear tool result and fall back to existing search/read tools.
- Preserve Stop cancellation and terminate Graph subprocesses through the existing sandbox command mechanism.
- Never recreate a healthy sandbox merely to enable Graph.

Update the existing explore, debug, review, and implementation skills to use Graph when helpful. Keep the current compact activity UI, with labels such as “Finding relevant code” and “Checking affected code.”

## 3. CFO.ai: scoped financial planning through MCP

### Connection and user experience

Use the official `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` endpoint through the existing MCP transport and OAuth implementation. The endpoint and workspace-selection procedure are documented by [CFO.ai](https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server).

Add CFO.ai to the **Business** plugin category after live qualification:

1. User connects through the existing OAuth flow.
2. AgentForge retrieves available CFO.ai workspaces.
3. User selects the workspace; automatically select only when exactly one is available.
4. The connection shows its workspace and setup status.
5. Financial conversations retain an explicit workspace/scenario context.

Keep this within existing plugin settings and conversation plugin controls. Do not introduce a separate finance application or redesign the chat interface.

Add provider-specific API endpoints under the existing plugin/session routers for:

- Listing authorized CFO.ai workspaces.
- Saving a connection’s workspace selection.
- Reading and changing a conversation’s finance context.

Responses contain identifiers, display names, setup state, and a context revision—never credentials. Existing generic plugin request/response fields remain compatible.

### Server-enforced scope

Add durable CFO.ai connection settings and conversation context records:

- A connection stores the chosen workspace and settings revision.
- A conversation stores the connection, workspace, selected scenario, and context revision.
- A new financial conversation inherits the connection’s selected workspace but does not create remote content immediately.
- The first requested write creates an AgentForge scenario through the normal approval path, then persists its returned identifier.
- Selecting Main must be a user action in the finance context controls. The model cannot switch into Main by supplying a different argument.
- Revalidate ownership, conversation selection, enabled tools, and context revision immediately before execution and after approval waits.
- Workspace changes invalidate pending finance approvals. Existing conversations require explicit rebinding rather than silently switching organizations.
- Apply the same provider policy to custom connections targeting the canonical CFO.ai endpoint, preventing a catalog-versus-custom bypass.

A scenario is not a private copy of connected data: it inherits Main updates, and connected sources remain shared. Therefore, v1 excludes integration administration, triggers, permissions, and account management. [CFO.ai scenario semantics](https://docs.cfo.ai/scenarios/understand-scenarios)

### Tools and modeling guidance

Start with a reviewed allowlist covering:

- Model, table, page, scenario, history, and dimension inspection.
- Documentation and modeling-skill retrieval.
- Table/formula creation and updates.
- Scenario creation and comparison.
- Saved report pages and validated visualizations.

Do not automatically enable newly advertised tools. Scenario merging, destructive restore, forced deletion, public sharing, and integration management are outside the first release.

Before model writes, load CFO.ai’s modeling instructions and its `build-model` skill. Preserve the documented one-action-block argument structure. [CFO.ai agent instructions](https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions)

Implementation details:

- Preserve bounded initialization guidance and expose it as scoped provider context, below platform and user authority.
- Add an AgentForge financial-planning skill describing the inspect → model → compare → verify workflow.
- Discover actual authenticated schemas during qualification and retain sanitized contract fixtures. Test our schema sanitizer against those fixtures.
- Bind and validate `org_id` and scenario before computing approval summaries or operation fingerprints.
- Validate supported action blocks server-side. Read/write classification must follow the reviewed provider policy rather than relying solely on `readOnlyHint`.
- Preserve normalized structured receipts and complete bounded tool results in owner-scoped storage; return a short preview plus a retrievable resource reference.
- Require read-back verification before claiming that a model, formula, scenario, or report was saved successfully.

### Reliable writes and OAuth

Add a CFO.ai operation journal containing operation identity, owner, conversation, effective workspace/scenario, argument digest, status, and private receipt references.

- Replayed completed operations return their recorded receipt.
- Serialize AgentForge writes to the same workspace/scenario across workers, with bounded leases and fencing.
- Timeouts or disconnects after dispatch become **outcome unknown**, not automatically retryable failures.
- Reconcile uncertain operations through available inspection/history tools. If the effect cannot be determined, stop further dependent writes and report the uncertainty.
- Do not promise exactly-once remote execution when the upstream service provides no verified idempotency contract.
- Cancellation stops further requests but must not claim it undid an already accepted remote write.
- Coordinate OAuth refresh across processes; the existing in-process lock and compare-and-swap save alone do not prevent simultaneous refresh requests.

Retain PKCE, browser-bound state, exact callback validation, issuer/resource binding, encrypted token storage, and SSRF protections. Validate these against the [MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization).

## 4. Trustworthy economics and the hackathon use case

### Correct the existing report

Extend [business_metrics.py](/Users/ashish/code/AgentForge/apps/api/src/agentforge/operations/business_metrics.py:13) with an explicitly versioned report format.

Separate:

- Provider-reported costs.
- Costs estimated from reported usage and configured rates.
- Conservative authorized upper bounds.
- Pending or unknown usage.
- External costs not represented in the tool ledger.

Classify recorded operations using `usage_json.cost_source` and recording state, not merely whether `cost_usd` is null. Preserve budget enforcement and settlement semantics.

Add daily totals, task outcomes, sample sizes, model/token breakdowns, retries, and cost distributions. Derive “cost per successful task” with failed attempts included in the stated numerator. Distinguish complete totals from partial coverage.

Keep the cross-user report operator-only. Ordinary CFO.ai users supply their own business assumptions and authorized data; connecting CFO.ai never grants access to AgentForge’s company-wide database.

### Capture missing sandbox costs

Record sandbox identity, conversation ownership, template resources, and lifecycle observations. Add authenticated, deduplicated lifecycle-event ingestion and reconciliation for missed/out-of-order events.

- Estimate compute from running intervals and configured effective-date rates.
- Include idle-running time; command duration alone is insufficient.
- Do not double-count a shared conversation sandbox across tools or subagents.
- Flag incomplete intervals and provider reconciliation differences.
- Import hosting, payment fees, subscriptions, support, and other overhead as separately labeled operator inputs.
- Treat unavailable plugin charges as unknown or externally billed, not established zero cost.

E2B bills for allocated compute while a sandbox is running, and its lifecycle webhooks support event-based tracking. [Billing](https://docs.e2b.dev/billing), [Lifecycle events](https://docs.e2b.dev/sandbox/lifecycle-events-webhooks)

### CFO.ai deliverable

Create an AgentForge business-plan workflow producing:

- A monthly 12-month model.
- Base, downside, and growth scenarios.
- Subscription-plus-usage versus usage-based pricing comparisons.
- Revenue, variable costs, gross margin, operating expenses, cash, and runway.
- Sensitivity to heavy usage, retries, model prices, and customer growth.
- A saved CFO.ai page showing assumptions, data dates, coverage limitations, and calculated results.

Use decimal currency values and deterministic arithmetic checks against selected model outputs. Zero revenue and nonpositive cash burn must produce meaningful “not applicable” results rather than misleading percentages or runway values.

For the demo, compare the same coding task with Graph disabled and enabled, then feed the measured difference into the financial scenarios. Use actual results—even if they show a tradeoff rather than an improvement.

## 5. Validation, rollout, and release criteria

### Implementation sequence

1. **Compatibility and baseline:** preserve existing work, capture authenticated CFO.ai contracts, qualify the pinned Graph binaries, and record current regression results.
2. **Graph integration:** introduce the template and typed tools behind a feature flag; verify source freshness, fallback, and existing sandbox behavior.
3. **CFO.ai integration:** add connection/context storage, modeling guidance, provider policy, operation receipts, and UI controls.
4. **Economics:** correct report provenance, add lifecycle accounting, and produce the CFO.ai business model.
5. **Qualification and evidence:** run regression, live-provider, browser, deployment, and before/after evaluations.

Use additive migrations, nullable/defaulted fields for existing connections, and independent feature flags. Apply migrations before enabling features. Do not rewrite existing conversation history, agent snapshots, budget records, or plugin selections.

### Required test matrix

| Area | Required scenarios |
|---|---|
| Graph correctness | Python/TypeScript fixtures, ambiguous symbols, current edits, deleted files, unsupported languages, partial coverage |
| Graph containment | Shell injection, path traversal, symlinks, hostile Git configuration, excluded secrets, oversized repositories |
| Graph lifecycle | Missing binary, incompatible version, timeout, Stop, reconnect, expired sandbox, repository switch, concurrent edits |
| CFO.ai authorization | Two users, multiple workspaces, tampered IDs, removed access, disconnected plugin, pending approval after scope change |
| CFO.ai modeling | One action block, large schemas, truncated previews, preserved receipts, correct scenario, formula read-back |
| CFO.ai reliability | Duplicate execution, concurrent writes, worker crash before/after dispatch, ambiguous timeout, cancellation, token rotation |
| Economics | Upper bounds versus estimates, unknown costs, running versus paused time, duplicate lifecycle events, task/subagent double counting |
| Existing product | GitHub login, repository access, shell/edit tools, PR delivery, plugins, skills, subagents, approvals, queues, Stop/Resume, streaming |

Run the existing release checks on the integrated change, including disposable-database migrations, frontend lint/types/build, and relevant UI tests. Run authenticated browser tests for connection, workspace selection, approvals, scenario switching, read-back, and reconnect.

### Production gates

Enable each integration only after:

- Its offline and live qualification checks pass.
- A real CFO.ai account completes OAuth, authorized inspection, scenario creation, formula update, and read-back.
- The new E2B template successfully analyzes a real repository without altering its publishable diff.
- Feature-disabled behavior matches the existing product.
- Missing or failed integrations do not prevent ordinary conversations.
- Structured logs distinguish rejected, failed, cancelled, and unknown operations without exposing credentials or financial content.
- Rollback is verified: disable the integration flags, retain durable receipts, and restore the previous template for new sandboxes without destroying existing work.

For evidence, run a fixed suite of at least ten coding tasks, three repetitions per configuration, with identical model settings and starting source. Report correctness, latency, tokens, tool calls, failures, and estimated total cost, including Graph analysis overhead. Preserve raw measurements and reviewed trace links; do not adopt vendor savings claims as AgentForge results.

Use a stable HTTPS origin for production OAuth. Keep the current Cloudflare tunnel unchanged during local implementation. Public deployment and authenticated live tests remain separate release gates.

**Completion means both integrations work through the normal user flow, their failure paths are qualified, existing functionality passes regression checks, and the hackathon claims are supported by inspectable evidence.**
</proposed_plan>

+# Entire Graph and CFO.ai
+
+These are independent, opt-in integrations. Existing chat, GitHub, sandbox, and plugin behavior remain usable with both flags off.
+No global tools are installed on the operator's computer. Runtime binaries are built into a separate E2B image.
+
+## Enable after qualification
+
+Apply Alembic migration `0020_finance_integrations` before enabling CFO.ai or importing usage events. It adds tables and does not
+rewrite existing conversations, credentials, approvals, budget operations, or immutable agent definitions. New built-in tasks
+use agent v4; versions 1–3 remain available for historical tasks.
+
+| Setting | Default | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `ENTIRE_GRAPH_ENABLED` | false | Offer three graph tools when a repository and E2B are available |
+| `ENTIRE_GRAPH_TIMEOUT_SEC` | 60 | Analysis deadline; normal source-search tools remain available on failure |
+| `CFO_AI_ENABLED` | false | Expose CFO.ai in the plugin catalog and permit its scoped runtime tools |
+| `E2B_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | unset | Verify E2B lifecycle events; without it the usage webhook is unavailable |
+
+Use a stable HTTPS production origin for OAuth. The current development tunnel does not need to be restarted or replaced.
+Turning off a flag rolls back access to the new integration; it does not erase the remote workspace or local receipts.
+
+## Entire Graph
+
+The tools are `code_graph_search`, `code_graph_symbol`, and `code_graph_impact`. They run trusted, pinned binaries against a
+bounded, no-follow temporary copy of the current workspace. The original workspace and its Git metadata are not modified.
+The helper checks content fingerprints again after analysis, retries a changed view once, and otherwise fails with ordinary
+search as fallback. Source is evidence, not instructions. Graph output is heuristic and coverage can be incomplete.
+
+The image pins Entire CLI `v0.11.4` and Graph `v0.4.1-nightly.202609240616.f22e6c95` by release archive SHA-256. The latter is a
+nightly candidate, not a claim of upstream stable support. Review the pinned source and requalify any upgrade. The adapter checks
+the installed Graph build before using it. Upstream history, transcripts, checkpoints, Entire hosting, and Brain are not enabled.
+
+Build and test explicitly (the build and canary create paid remote resources):
+
+```sh
+BUILD_ENTIRE_GRAPH=1 apps/api/.venv/bin/python infra/e2b/template.py
+cd apps/api
+.venv/bin/python examples/entire_graph_canary.py --template TEMPLATE_ID
+```
+
+Record the template ID, build ID, binary versions, helper source revision, and canary output before choosing `E2B_TEMPLATE_ID`.
+Existing sandboxes are not replaced: those without the helper fall back to normal search. The canary always kills its temporary
+sandbox. It covers Python source discovery, symbols, impact, and edits; it does not establish model accuracy or token savings.
+
+References: [Graph commands](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/main/docs/commands.md),
+[cache semantics](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/main/docs/operations.md),
+[security boundaries](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/main/docs/trust-and-security.md).

+## CFO.ai
+
+The official remote MCP server is `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`. Each person connects their own account through existing OAuth.
+Choose the workspace in Settings → Plugins → CFO.ai. In a selected conversation, Finance chooses the scenario. Main requires
+pressing **Use Main**. New alternative scenarios are created only as an approved financial write, not when a conversation opens.
+
+The first write requires reading CFO.ai's `build-model` instructions. The packaged financial-planning skill describes a 12-month
+model, base/downside/growth alternatives, saved reports, formula checks, and read-back verification. Each verified scenario
+creation selects the new scenario; earlier scenarios created by the conversation remain readable for comparison.
+
+The integration binds workspace/scenario before approvals and rechecks them before execution. Changing the workspace or scenario
+invalidates prepared calls. Ask me asks; Approve for me runs permitted changes. Read-only subagents are never given write tools.
+The curated policy excludes account/integration administration, triggers, merging, restoring, forced deletion, and public sharing.
+Custom connections to the canonical CFO.ai endpoint receive the same policy.
+
+Server initialization guidance is bounded, provider-scoped data. MCP result previews remain short; complete results up to 200 KB
+are retained in existing owner-scoped context resources. Unknown tools stay disabled, irrespective of upstream annotations.
+
+### Unknown write outcomes
+
+A PostgreSQL transaction lock serializes writes to a workspace/scenario across workers. A durable receipt is written before
+dispatch. A repeated completed operation returns its receipt. Timeouts, cancellation after dispatch, unexpected remote errors,
+and lost receipts block dependent writes rather than blindly retrying. Token refresh also uses a cross-process transaction lock.
+No exactly-once guarantee is claimed for the remote service.
+
+After inspecting CFO.ai history and verifying the actual outcome, an operator can record the resolution without repeating the write:

+```sh

+  --outcome applied --evidence 'private history/version reference'
+```

+uses a new operation identity. The receipt is an operator assertion backed by the supplied reference, not a fabricated vendor receipt.
+

+
+OAuth metadata discovery works, but a user must create a CFO.ai account and authorize access before live tools can be qualified.
+Keep `CFO_AI_ENABLED=false` in production until a disposable workspace passes authentication, organization/scenario listing,
+model-skill loading, scenario creation, formula updates, read-back, token renewal, and reconnect tests. The collection parser accepts
+explicit structured JSON envelopes and rejects prose IDs. Capture sanitized real schemas and receipts to check for vendor drift;
+the offline smoke test uses synthetic responses and does not replace this gate.
+
+References: [MCP server](https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server),
+[modeling instructions](https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions),
+[scenario behavior](https://docs.cfo.ai/scenarios/understand-scenarios).
+
+## Costs and business evidence
+
+`business_metrics` now exports schema v2. It separates adapter-reported costs, configured-rate estimates, authorized upper bounds,
+and unmeasured operations. A non-null ledger amount is not automatically a measured charge. Reports include cohort counts, daily
+totals, distributions, and conservative cost per successful task, including failed-attempt costs. They never expose prompts,
+repository names, user IDs, or task IDs. This remains an operator-only command, not an ordinary agent capability.
+
+E2B sends signed lifecycle events to `/api/v1/sandbox-usage/webhook`. Use a dedicated signature secret and subscribe to created,
+resumed, paused, killed, updated, and checkpointed events. Receipt IDs deduplicate delivery retries. Only whitelisted metadata is
+stored. API reconciliation accepts the provider's camelCase envelope as well as the documented webhook snake_case envelope.

+  --external-costs /private/assumptions.json --output /private/agentforge-costs.json

+
+The optional assumptions file is a JSON object with `currency: "USD"`, `monthly_costs` (category → decimal string),
+`cash_balance`, and optional `sandbox_rates` (`effective_from`, `vcpu_usd_per_second`, `gib_usd_per_second`). Supply real rates and
